edits.current: "checked-record": "Pass only payload fields: Interval {lo, hi}, Triple {data} for Sized 3, and Percent {value} for Bounded 0 101. The generated adapter applies the exact constructor selected for Packet and its nested Word field through direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value branch. C callers initialize and clear generated records and owning results; C++ callers use Packet values, vectors, optionals, products, results, Holder and Choice. Rejected inputs leave the complete caller graph and existing C output unchanged, and later valid calls recover. Array and Option results contain proof-free Packet payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices remain authenticated type metadata rather than host fields. The generated C/GMP, C++ multiprecision, C# BigInteger, Java BigInteger and Kotlin BigInteger records expose only proof-free payloads. Full packages validate all eight indexed inputs through the exact selected Lean constructors, preserve rejected caller values, recover on the next valid call and return all eight proof-free results. Standalone result-only packages expose the same results without checked-input metadata. Proof-only Witness crosses as a nominal empty carrier; C uses one non-semantic uint8_t storage byte solely to give the structure a legal nonzero size, while C++ uses an empty structure. Token keeps its Unit field, plain empty Marker remains an ordinary empty record, and Option presence, arrays, and the active or inactive Mark branches remain distinct. Full packages validate nullary checked constructors and exact rejection and recovery. Result-only packages project Lean-produced proof-erased values without input-constructor metadata. The proof-free host value carries bound and below as payload fields. Full packages validate each host input through the selected DependentRecords.mkDependent constructor, which rejects below >= bound before Lean code runs, preserve rejected caller values and return the exact proof-free result. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced results without checked-input metadata."

Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. edits.current: "checked-record": "Pass only payload fields: Interval {lo, hi}, Triple {data} for Sized 3, and Percent {value} for Bounded 0 101. The generated adapter applies the exact constructor selected for Packet and its nested Word field through direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value branch. C callers initialize and clear generated records and owning results; C++ callers use Packet values, vectors, optionals, products, results, Holder and Choice. Rejected inputs leave the complete caller graph and existing C output unchanged, and later valid calls recover. Array and Option results contain proof-free Packet payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. Repeated parameters keep independent constructor choices; later valid calls recover. Copied Array and Option results contain the same nested payload objects without proof fields or input-constructor selection. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Standalone result-only packages return the same proof-free objects without input-constructor metadata. edits.current: "checked-record": "Pass only payload fields: Interval {lo, hi}, Triple {data} for Sized 3, and Percent {value} for Bounded 0 101. Input constructors validate cross-field predicates or normalize values inside Lean without changing caller input. Results expose payload fields, not proofs. A standalone result-only package works without any checked input. Generic records, other indices and dynamic dependent payloads are not covered. Packet is a proof-free object with digit: bigint for Fin 10 and word: bigint for a checked Nat Subtype. The selected adapter descends through Array, List, Option, Product, Except, enclosing Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value field, applies the exact constructor selected for every public site and nested Word field, and leaves the caller's complete rejected graph unchanged. Repeated parameters keep independent constructor choices; later valid calls recover. Copied Array and Option results contain the same nested payload objects without proof fields or input-constructor selection. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices stay in authenticated type metadata and are not host fields. JavaScript and TypeScript pass proof-free objects: On, Off, EmptyToken, UnicodeToken, ZeroToken and WideToken expose count: bigint; Ab exposes size: bigint; EmptySized exposes data: bigint[]. The full package checks records indexed by both booleans, \"ab\", the empty string, \"λ🌱\", zero and 340282366920938463463374607431768211457 through the exact selected Lean constructors, preserves rejected caller values and recovers on the next valid call. Standalone result-only packages return the same proof-free objects without input-constructor metadata. Proof-only Witness crosses as an owned JavaScript object with no payload properties and as Readonly<Record<PropertyKey, never>> in TypeScript. Token keeps its Unit field, plain empty Marker remains distinct, Option presence, array length and active or inactive Mark branches remain explicit. Full packages validate the nullary checked constructor and exact rejection and recovery; result-only packages project Lean-produced proof-erased values without input-constructor metadata. The proof-free host value carries bound and below as payload fields. Full packages validate each host input through the selected DependentRecords.mkDependent constructor, which rejects below >= bound before Lean code runs, preserve rejected caller values and return the exact proof-free result. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced results without checked-input metadata."

Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices remain authenticated metadata rather than Python dataclass fields. Generated frozen records use exact Python int values for `count`, `size` and every `EmptySized.data` element. Full wheels exercise exact per-site constructors, negative-Nat host refusal, unchanged rejected values, recovery and proof-free results; standalone result-only wheels expose the same copied records without checked-input metadata. Proof-only Witness crosses as a frozen, slotted Python dataclass with no fields. Token retains tag: None, Marker remains a distinct frozen dataclass, Some(Witness()) stays distinct from None, and sequences retain their length and Mark branch. Full wheels validate exact classes, the nullary constructor and recovery; result-only wheels project Lean-produced proof-erased values without input-constructor metadata. The proof-free host value carries bound and below as payload fields. Full packages validate each host input through the selected DependentRecords.mkDependent constructor, which rejects below >= bound before Lean code runs, preserve rejected caller values and return the exact proof-free result. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced results without checked-input metadata."

edits.current: "checked-record": "Pass the generated record's runtime payload fields, without proof values. The selected Lean constructor checks each input and may normalize it; rejection identifies the parameter and constructor and preserves caller data. Results contain copied payload fields with proofs erased. Both ordinary and independently reviewed packages, including standalone result-only packages, passed installed checks. The tested Rust Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as num_bigint::BigUint values. Holder nests Packet, and Choice::Packet carries it in the active Choice branch. Generated Rust adapters apply the exact Packet and nested Word constructors selected at each direct, repeated, Array, List, Option, tuple, Result, Holder and Choice input site. Rejected calls preserve the complete caller graph and later valid calls recover. Packet arrays and options returned by Lean contain proof-free payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices remain authenticated metadata rather than Rust record fields. Generated structs use BigUint for Nat payloads such as `count`, `size` and every `EmptySized.data` element. Full crates exercise exact per-site constructors, unchanged rejected values, recovery and proof-free results; standalone result-only crates expose the same copied records without checked-input metadata. Proof-only Witness crosses as a nominal empty Rust struct with no application payload. Token keeps its generated Unit field, plain empty Marker remains a distinct nominal struct, Option presence stays explicit, vectors retain length and independent elements, and active or inactive Mark branches remain distinct. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices remain authenticated type metadata rather than host fields. The generated C/GMP, C++ multiprecision, C# BigInteger, Java BigInteger and Kotlin BigInteger records expose only proof-free payloads. Full packages validate all eight indexed inputs through the exact selected Lean constructors, preserve rejected caller values, recover on the next valid call and return all eight proof-free results. Standalone result-only packages expose the same results without checked-input metadata. Proof-only Witness crosses as a nominal, non-null JVM object with no application payload: Java exposes a zero-component record and Kotlin a zero-property class. Token keeps its generated Unit member, plain empty Marker remains a distinct nominal type, Option presence stays explicit, arrays retain length and independent elements, and active or inactive Mark branches remain distinct. Full packages validate nullary checked constructors and exact rejection and recovery. Result-only packages project Lean-produced proof-erased values without input-constructor metadata. The proof-free host value carries bound and below as payload fields. Full packages validate each host input through the selected DependentRecords.mkDependent constructor, which rejects below >= bound before Lean code runs, preserve rejected caller values and return the exact proof-free result. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced results without checked-input metadata."

Author sources are removed before offline installation; Java and Kotlin callers replay after moving the installed tree and execute again after deleting all consumer sources, giving six executions per selection. Compiler probes check the generated API, Java and Kotlin Unit classes, Kotlin function references and result nullability. The full API checks direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, both Except branches, Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value field, including exact per-site constructors, normalization, complete rejected-input snapshots and recovery. Independent controls reject every missing or changed retained record and coordinated resource, model, package, probe and execution mutations. Checked-record JVM acceptance covers the established top-level Interval, Sized 3 and Bounded 0 101 forms plus the tested acyclic Packet, Holder and Choice forms through Array, List, Option, Product and Except copied positions. Generic records, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Both author routes and full/result-only APIs reproduce complete Maven packages from two author roots, remove author sources, install offline, replay after relocation and execute again after deleting all consumer sources. The runs use JDK 22.0.2, Kotlin 2.2.0 and Lean 4.32.2 on Linux x64/glibc 2.36 with an explicit 2.36 package floor and 64-bit machine words. Original receipts, retained package members, compiler probes, execution records and selected sources are archived; native libraries and the closed JAR retain exact identities without copied bytes. Constructor entry counts and peak memory are unmeasured. Hosted glibc 2.38 release-floor acceptance remains assigned to the recurring workflow. Additional inherited jvm acceptance: The jvm installed lane authenticates the ordinary full inherited checked-record package selection for java, kotlin. The full API checks valid, normalized, invalid parent, invalid child, alias, nested Fin, repeated-constructor and recovery cases before projecting proof-free results. Two independent author builds, source removal, offline installation, relocation and unchanged caller replay are retained where the host permits them. The fixture covers inherited parent subobjects, child checked fields, aliases, nested inheritance, repeated constructor selections, and constructor-free results. Ordinary and independently reviewed sources are exercised in full and result-only Maven packages through independent Java and Kotlin callers. Complete Maven packages are reproduced, installed offline, executed before and after relocation, and reduced to source-free runtime deployments. Complete package archives, receipts, inventories, probes, execution records, TAP, controls, and producer/checker/archive source closures are retained. The package floor is glibc 2.38; the archive records and verifies the hosted runner's independently observed glibc and JVM tool identities. Compiler, operating-system, JDK, Kotlin compiler, Maven-format archive, and glibc distributions remain trusted inputs. This archive establishes installed JVM behavior, not promotion into the public support inventory. Inherited checked-record acceptance covers only the tested acyclic Span → Ticket → Stamped chain, its Ticket alias, repeated direct parameters, nested parent constraints and proof-free Ticket/Stamped results. Value-carrying receiver-dependent inherited fields, generic or recursive inheritance, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Additional recursive jvm acceptance: The jvm installed lane authenticates the ordinary mutual recursive checked-record selection for java, kotlin. Original inputs, exact failures, preserved rejected values, recovery and proof-free results are retained; independently reproduced packages are installed without author sources and replayed after relocation where the host permits it. The archive authenticates local Linux x64/glibc 2.36 acceptance; it does not claim hosted-runner acceptance or promote support before the whole recursive-record matrix closes. Both ordinary source and independently reviewed Binding IR routes reproduce complete Maven packages from two isolated author roots, remove author sources, install offline, relocate, and replay without consumer sources. Each route runs the unchanged typed Java caller and route-bound Kotlin caller three times. Java records 590 checks, 72 native rejections, five host rejections, 290 calls and snapshots, 77 recoveries and 64 rounds per execution; Kotlin records 593 checks, 72 native rejections, six host rejections, 292 calls and snapshots, 78 recoveries and 64 rounds. The fixture covers mutually recursive records and variants, transparent aliases, active Option and variant branches, exact Subtype and Fin failures, null carriers, cycles, depth limits, immutable callers, and constructor-free results. Kotlin additionally proves three compile-time non-null rejections through positive and negative compiler controls; Java proves its record carriers refuse cycle construction before runtime traversal. The original JARs and POMs, receipts, generated-source identities, nullability diagnostics, execution records, and selected producer/checker sources are retained. The complete JDK and Kotlin distribution remain trusted external tools represented by recorded identities. Recursive checked-record acceptance covers the tested Packet self-cycle and Envelope ↔ Step mutual cycle, their aliases, Array/Option wrappers, active branches, Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields in copied parameters, results and fields. It does not establish generic recursive records, other recursive graph shapes, value-carrying receiver-dependent fields, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks or owned positions. Additional hosted closed-index acceptance: Hosted GitHub Actions run 39213054169 rebuilt the full ordinary-source java/kotlin package selection on Ubuntu 24.04. Two author roots reproduce the complete package, remove author sources, install without network access, relocate the installed tree and replay unchanged typed callers. The full API exercises all eight checked inputs, exact constructor failures, unchanged rejected values, recovery and all eight proof-free indexed results. The retained archive authenticates every original artifact byte, route result, package, caller observation and selected source. Hosted value-index acceptance covers only the retained top-level copied checked-record parameter and result sites with closed Bool, String and Nat indices. Full packages cover parameters and results; standalone result-only packages cover results only. Open or opaque indices; Int, Char, fixed-width and platform-width integers, Fin, functions, proofs, instances and other index kinds; checked-record fields, callbacks and owned positions; value-carrying dependent payloads; and zero-payload checked records remain unreviewed here. The archives retain original hosted records, complete packages, reports, caller observations and exact source closures. External Lean, C/C++, .NET, Java, Kotlin, linker and operating-system toolchains remain trusted recorded inputs. Additional hosted zero-payload Java/Kotlin acceptance: Hosted GitHub Actions run 39561655653 rebuilt the ordinary-source Java and Kotlin Maven package selection on Ubuntu 24.04. Two author roots reproduced the complete package before author removal, source-free offline installation and unchanged replay after physical relocation. The full package runs the selected nullary Witness constructor at every checked input, keeps rejected values unchanged, recovers on the next valid call and projects proof-erased Witness, Token, Marker, Option, Array and Mark results. The retained archive authenticates every original artifact byte, route result, caller observation and exact producer, consumer, checker and archiver source closure. Hosted zero-payload Java/Kotlin acceptance covers the retained Witness, Token, Marker, Option, Array and Mark fixtures at copied parameter and result sites in four ordinary/reviewed full/result-only Maven packages. It does not promote checked-record fields, callbacks, owned positions, other zero-payload shapes or another host. External Lean, Java, Kotlin and operating-system toolchains remain trusted recorded inputs."

Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. Proof-only Witness crosses as a guarded zero-argument readonly PHP class. Token retains its null Unit field, Marker remains a distinct readonly class, and Option presence, list length and both Mark branches remain distinct. edits.current: "checked-record": "Pass the generated record's runtime payload fields, without proof values. The selected Lean constructor checks each input and may normalize it; rejection identifies the parameter and constructor and preserves caller data. Results contain copied payload fields with proofs erased. Both ordinary and independently reviewed packages, including standalone result-only packages, passed installed checks. The tested Component Model Packet is a WIT record whose Fin 10 digit and checked Nat Subtype word are canonical list<u32> limbs. A Holder record nests Packet, and the packet case of Choice carries it in its active branch. Generated WIT adapters apply the exact Packet and nested Word constructors selected at each direct, repeated, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder and Choice input site. Rejected calls preserve the complete caller value tree and output sentinel, and later valid calls recover. Packet arrays and options returned by Lean contain proof-free WIT records without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices remain authenticated metadata rather than WIT record fields. Generated records expose Nat payloads such as `count`, `size` and every `EmptySized.data` element as exact little-endian `list<u32>` limbs. Full components exercise exact per-site constructors, malformed-Nat host refusal, unchanged rejected values, recovery and proof-free results; standalone result-only components expose the same copied records without checked-input metadata. Proof-only Witness follows the generator's WIT empty-carrier convention as enum witness { empty }; this is a representation choice, not a Lean semantic distinction. Token remains record token { tag: unit }, Marker uses its own empty enum, option presence, list length and Mark branches remain explicit. Full component packages validate the nullary checked constructor and recovery; result-only packages project Lean-produced proof-erased values without input-constructor metadata. The proof-free host value carries bound and below as payload fields. Full packages validate each host input through the selected DependentRecords.mkDependent constructor, which rejects below >= bound before Lean code runs, preserve rejected caller values and return the exact proof-free result. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced results without checked-input metadata."

Author roots are removed before offline installation; the unchanged public C caller is compiled once, its source is removed, and the resulting executable runs before and after moving the complete installed tree, giving two executions per selection. The full API checks direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, both Except branches, Holder.packet and the active Choice packet value field, including exact per-site constructors, normalization, complete rejected-input snapshots and recovery. Checked-record WIT/WASI acceptance covers the established top-level Interval, Sized 3 and Bounded 0 101 forms plus the tested acyclic Packet, Holder and Choice forms through Array, List, Option, Product and Except copied positions. Generic checked records, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Both author routes and full/result-only APIs reproduce complete WIT component archives from two author roots, remove author roots, install offline, compile one unchanged public C caller, remove its source, and execute it before and after physically relocating each installation. The compiler-free runs use Wasmtime 42.0.1 and wasm-tools 1.245.1 on Linux x64/glibc 2.36 with an explicit 2.36 package floor, 64-bit native machine words and a recorded 20.0 host-load admission ceiling. The component requires its packaged native Lean host and is not a standalone WASI command. The archive retains complete handoff archives, extracted package records, receipts, installed inventories, execution records and both producer and verifier source closures. GCC, wasm-tools and Wasmtime remain trusted toolchain inputs. Hosted glibc 2.38 release-floor acceptance remains assigned to the dedicated workflow. Constructor dispatch and peak memory are unmeasured. Additional inherited wit acceptance: The wit installed lane authenticates the reviewed full inherited checked-record package selection for wit-wasi. The full API checks valid, normalized, invalid parent, invalid child, alias, nested Fin, repeated-constructor and recovery cases before projecting proof-free results. Two independent author builds, source removal, offline installation, relocation and unchanged caller replay are retained where the host permits them. The fixture covers inherited parent subobjects, child checked fields, aliases, nested inheritance, repeated constructor selections, and constructor-free results. Ordinary and independently reviewed sources are exercised in full and result-only WIT/WASI component packages. Complete packages are reproduced from two author roots, installed offline, exercised before and after relocation, and checked at a glibc 2.38 release floor. The generated C host requires its packaged native Lean component runtime; it is not a standalone WASI command. Complete archives, receipts, source-free inventories, caller binaries, execution records, TAP, and producer/checker/archive source closures are retained. Compiler, operating-system, wasm-tools, Wasmtime, and C toolchain distributions remain trusted inputs. This archive establishes installed WIT/WASI behavior, not promotion into the public support inventory. Inherited checked-record acceptance covers only the tested acyclic Span → Ticket → Stamped chain, its Ticket alias, repeated direct parameters, nested parent constraints and proof-free Ticket/Stamped results. Value-carrying receiver-dependent inherited fields, generic or recursive inheritance, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Additional recursive wit acceptance: The wit installed lane authenticates the reviewed recursive recursive checked-record selection for wit-wasi. Original inputs, exact failures, preserved rejected values, recovery and proof-free results are retained; independently reproduced packages are installed without author sources and replayed after relocation where the host permits it. The fixtures cover self-recursive Packet and mutual Envelope/Step groups with Option and Array carriers. Checked fields are limited to Fin 3 and the tested plusOne/plusTwo Nat Subtype constructors. Each package is a copied-graph WIT component whose native host forwards exact refinement diagnostics as the final Wasmtime error cause; callbacks, resources and owned positions remain separate work. The component requires its packaged native Lean host and is not a standalone WASI command. Accepted cells come from serial attempts r2 and r3 at one frozen revision; r1 and the r2 reviewed-mutual cell refused on disk and load guards and are retained only as observations. These local Linux x64/glibc 2.36 runs do not establish hosted release-floor acceptance. Constructor dispatch and peak memory are unmeasured. Recursive checked-record acceptance covers the tested Packet self-cycle and Envelope ↔ Step mutual cycle, their aliases, Array/Option wrappers, active branches, Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields in copied parameters, results and fields. It does not establish generic recursive records, other recursive graph shapes, value-carrying receiver-dependent fields, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks or owned positions. The wit installed lane authenticates the reviewed mutual recursive checked-record selection for wit-wasi. Original inputs, exact failures, preserved rejected values, recovery and proof-free results are retained; independently reproduced packages are installed without author sources and replayed after relocation where the host permits it. The fixtures cover self-recursive Packet and mutual Envelope/Step groups with Option and Array carriers. Checked fields are limited to Fin 3 and the tested plusOne/plusTwo Nat Subtype constructors. Each package is a copied-graph WIT component whose native host forwards exact refinement diagnostics as the final Wasmtime error cause; callbacks, resources and owned positions remain separate work. The component requires its packaged native Lean host and is not a standalone WASI command. Accepted cells come from serial attempts r2 and r3 at one frozen revision; r1 and the r2 reviewed-mutual cell refused on disk and load guards and are retained only as observations. These local Linux x64/glibc 2.36 runs do not establish hosted release-floor acceptance. Constructor dispatch and peak memory are unmeasured. Recursive checked-record acceptance covers the tested Packet self-cycle and Envelope ↔ Step mutual cycle, their aliases, Array/Option wrappers, active branches, Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields in copied parameters, results and fields. It does not establish generic recursive records, other recursive graph shapes, value-carrying receiver-dependent fields, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks or owned positions. Additional hosted closed-index acceptance: Hosted GitHub Actions run 39373895062 rebuilt this full reviewed-ir WIT/WASI component selection on Ubuntu 24.04. Two author roots reproduce the complete component archive, remove author roots, install offline, compile one unchanged public C caller, remove its source, relocate the installation and replay its binary through Wasmtime. The full API exercises all eight checked inputs, exact constructor refusals, unchanged rejected values, recovery and all eight proof-free indexed results. The archive authenticates the original workflow, job, artifact, toolchain log, TAP, reports, package receipt, component archive and exact source identities. Hosted WIT/WASI value-index acceptance covers only the archived top-level copied checked-record parameter and result sites with closed Bool, String and Nat indices. Full components cover parameters and results; standalone result-only components cover results only. Open or opaque indices; Int, Char, fixed-width and platform-width integers, Fin, functions, proofs, instances and other index kinds; checked-record fields, callbacks and owned positions; value-carrying dependent payloads; and zero-payload checked records remain unreviewed here. The run covers source-free installation and relocated replay through Wasmtime 42.0.1 and wasm-tools 1.245.1 on Ubuntu 24.04, Linux x64/glibc 2.39 with a glibc 2.38 package floor. Each component requires its packaged native Lean host and is not a standalone WASI command. Complete component archives, receipts, generated projections, caller binaries, reports, execution records, original workflow records and source closures are retained; external Lean, Nix, C, wasm-tools, Wasmtime and operating-system toolchains remain trusted recorded inputs. Other host targets require separate installed evidence. Additional hosted zero-payload WIT/WASI acceptance: Hosted GitHub Actions run 39588427412 rebuilt the reviewed-ir WIT/WASI selection on Ubuntu 24.04. Two independent author roots reproduced the complete prepared package before author removal, source-free offline installation and unchanged replay after physical relocation. The package runs the selected nullary Witness constructor at every checked input, keeps rejected values unchanged, recovers on the next valid call and projects proof-erased results. The retained archive authenticates every original artifact byte, route result, caller observation and exact producer, consumer, checker and archiver source closure. Hosted zero-payload WIT/WASI acceptance covers only the retained Witness, Token, Marker, Option, Array and Mark fixtures at copied parameter and result sites in four ordinary/reviewed full/result-only packages. It does not promote checked-record fields, callbacks, owned positions, other zero-payload shapes, PHP-Wasm or another host. External Lean, consumer-language, package-manager and operating-system toolchains remain trusted recorded inputs. Additional hosted dependent acceptance: Hosted GitHub Actions run 39871962476, job 120148286417, artifact 12468135063 rebuilt the full reviewed-ir wit-wasi package selection. The author routes reproduce the package, remove author sources, install without network access and replay unchanged typed callers. The full API exercises valid and rejected dependent inputs through the selected constructor, unchanged rejected values, recovery and proof-free results. The retained archive authenticates every original artifact byte, route result, package, caller observation and selected source. Hosted dependent checked-record acceptance covers only the retained top-level copied DependentRecords.Dependent parameter and result sites, whose Fin bound field depends on the runtime bound field and whose proof is rebuilt by the selected mkDependent constructor. Full packages cover parameters and results; standalone result-only packages cover results only. Dependent fields of other kinds, nested or recursive dependent records, checked-record fields, callbacks, owned positions, open or opaque indices and zero-payload records remain unreviewed here. The PHP-Wasm cells are the shared result tracked by #1461 and are not inferred from native PHP. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs."

edits.current: "checked-record": "Pass the generated record's runtime payload fields, without proof values. The selected Lean constructor checks each input and may normalize it; rejection identifies the parameter and constructor and preserves caller data. Results contain copied payload fields with proofs erased. Both ordinary and independently reviewed packages, including standalone result-only packages, passed installed checks. The tested Component Model Packet is a WIT record whose Fin 10 digit and checked Nat Subtype word are canonical list<u32> limbs. A Holder record nests Packet, and the packet case of Choice carries it in its active branch. Generated WIT adapters apply the exact Packet and nested Word constructors selected at each direct, repeated, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder and Choice input site. Rejected calls preserve the complete caller value tree and output sentinel, and later valid calls recover. Packet arrays and options returned by Lean contain proof-free WIT records without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices remain authenticated metadata rather than WIT record fields. Generated records expose Nat payloads such as `count`, `size` and every `EmptySized.data` element as exact little-endian `list<u32>` limbs. Full components exercise exact per-site constructors, malformed-Nat host refusal, unchanged rejected values, recovery and proof-free results; standalone result-only components expose the same copied records without checked-input metadata. Proof-only Witness follows the generator's WIT empty-carrier convention as enum witness { empty }; this is a representation choice, not a Lean semantic distinction. Token remains record token { tag: unit }, Marker uses its own empty enum, option presence, list length and Mark branches remain explicit. Full component packages validate the nullary checked constructor and recovery; result-only packages project Lean-produced proof-erased values without input-constructor metadata. The proof-free host value carries bound and below as payload fields. Full packages validate each host input through the selected DependentRecords.mkDependent constructor, which rejects below >= bound before Lean code runs, preserve rejected caller values and return the exact proof-free result. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced results without checked-input metadata."

edits.current: "checked-record": "Pass generated record objects containing Math::BigInt values and plain array references, without proofs. Lean runs the selected constructor for each input; it may normalize accepted data, or reject with the parameter and constructor name while preserving caller values. Results contain independent copied payload fields with proofs erased. Ordinary and reviewed packages, including standalone result-only packages, passed installed checks. The tested Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as Math::BigInt values. Holder nests Packet, and Choice::Packet carries it in the active Choice branch. Generated Perl adapters apply the exact Packet and nested Word constructors selected at each direct, repeated, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder and Choice input site. Rejected calls preserve the complete caller graph and later valid calls recover. Packet arrays and options returned by Lean contain proof-free payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices remain authenticated metadata rather than Perl fields. Generated blessed records use `Math::BigInt` for `count`, `size` and every `EmptySized.data` element. Full packages exercise exact per-site constructors, negative-Nat host refusal, unchanged rejected values, recovery and proof-free results; standalone result-only packages expose the same copied records without checked-input metadata. Proof-only Witness crosses as an exact blessed Perl class backed by a plain empty hash. Token retains its Unit value, Marker remains a distinct blessed class, undef stays distinct from a present Witness, arrays retain length, and Mark keeps its branch. Full CPAN packages validate exact classes across four ABI interpreters, the nullary constructor and recovery; result-only packages project Lean-produced proof-erased values without input-constructor metadata. The proof-free host value carries bound and below as payload fields. Full packages validate each host input through the selected DependentRecords.mkDependent constructor, which rejects below >= bound before Lean code runs, preserve rejected caller values and return the exact proof-free result. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced results without checked-input metadata."

edits.current: "checked-record": "Pass generated record objects containing Math::BigInt values and plain array references, without proofs. Lean runs the selected constructor for each input; it may normalize accepted data, or reject with the parameter and constructor name while preserving caller values. Results contain independent copied payload fields with proofs erased. Ordinary and reviewed packages, including standalone result-only packages, passed installed checks. The tested Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as Math::BigInt values. Holder nests Packet, and Choice::Packet carries it in the active Choice branch. Generated Perl adapters apply the exact Packet and nested Word constructors selected at each direct, repeated, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder and Choice input site. Rejected calls preserve the complete caller graph and later valid calls recover. Packet arrays and options returned by Lean contain proof-free payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices remain authenticated metadata rather than Perl fields. Generated blessed records use `Math::BigInt` for `count`, `size` and every `EmptySized.data` element. Full packages exercise exact per-site constructors, negative-Nat host refusal, unchanged rejected values, recovery and proof-free results; standalone result-only packages expose the same copied records without checked-input metadata. Proof-only Witness crosses as an exact blessed Perl class backed by a plain empty hash. Token retains its Unit value, Marker remains a distinct blessed class, undef stays distinct from a present Witness, arrays retain length, and Mark keeps its branch. Full CPAN packages validate exact classes across four ABI interpreters, the nullary constructor and recovery; result-only packages project Lean-produced proof-erased values without input-constructor metadata. The proof-free host value carries bound and below as payload fields. Full packages validate each host input through the selected DependentRecords.mkDependent constructor, which rejects below >= bound before Lean code runs, preserve rejected caller values and return the exact proof-free result. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced results without checked-input metadata."

edits.current: "checked-record": "Pass generated record objects containing Math::BigInt values and plain array references, without proofs. Lean runs the selected constructor for each input; it may normalize accepted data, or reject with the parameter and constructor name while preserving caller values. Results contain independent copied payload fields with proofs erased. Ordinary and reviewed packages, including standalone result-only packages, passed installed checks. The tested Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as Math::BigInt values. Holder nests Packet, and Choice::Packet carries it in the active Choice branch. Generated Perl adapters apply the exact Packet and nested Word constructors selected at each direct, repeated, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder and Choice input site. Rejected calls preserve the complete caller graph and later valid calls recover. Packet arrays and options returned by Lean contain proof-free payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices remain authenticated metadata rather than Perl fields. Generated blessed records use `Math::BigInt` for `count`, `size` and every `EmptySized.data` element. Full packages exercise exact per-site constructors, negative-Nat host refusal, unchanged rejected values, recovery and proof-free results; standalone result-only packages expose the same copied records without checked-input metadata. Proof-only Witness crosses as an exact blessed Perl class backed by a plain empty hash. Token retains its Unit value, Marker remains a distinct blessed class, undef stays distinct from a present Witness, arrays retain length, and Mark keeps its branch. Full CPAN packages validate exact classes across four ABI interpreters, the nullary constructor and recovery; result-only packages project Lean-produced proof-erased values without input-constructor metadata. The proof-free host value carries bound and below as payload fields. Full packages validate each host input through the selected DependentRecords.mkDependent constructor, which rejects below >= bound before Lean code runs, preserve rejected caller values and return the exact proof-free result. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced results without checked-input metadata."

edits.current: "checked-record": "Pass generated record objects containing Math::BigInt values and plain array references, without proofs. Lean runs the selected constructor for each input; it may normalize accepted data, or reject with the parameter and constructor name while preserving caller values. Results contain independent copied payload fields with proofs erased. Ordinary and reviewed packages, including standalone result-only packages, passed installed checks. The tested Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as Math::BigInt values. Holder nests Packet, and Choice::Packet carries it in the active Choice branch. Generated Perl adapters apply the exact Packet and nested Word constructors selected at each direct, repeated, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder and Choice input site. Rejected calls preserve the complete caller graph and later valid calls recover. Packet arrays and options returned by Lean contain proof-free payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices remain authenticated metadata rather than Perl fields. Generated blessed records use `Math::BigInt` for `count`, `size` and every `EmptySized.data` element. Full packages exercise exact per-site constructors, negative-Nat host refusal, unchanged rejected values, recovery and proof-free results; standalone result-only packages expose the same copied records without checked-input metadata. Proof-only Witness crosses as an exact blessed Perl class backed by a plain empty hash. Token retains its Unit value, Marker remains a distinct blessed class, undef stays distinct from a present Witness, arrays retain length, and Mark keeps its branch. Full CPAN packages validate exact classes across four ABI interpreters, the nullary constructor and recovery; result-only packages project Lean-produced proof-erased values without input-constructor metadata. The proof-free host value carries bound and below as payload fields. Full packages validate each host input through the selected DependentRecords.mkDependent constructor, which rejects below >= bound before Lean code runs, preserve rejected caller values and return the exact proof-free result. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced results without checked-input metadata."

edits.current: "checked-record": "Pass only payload fields: Interval {lo, hi}, Triple {data} for Sized 3, and Percent {value} for Bounded 0 101, using bigint and bigint[] values. The selected Lean constructor checks or normalizes each input; constructor rejection identifies the parameter and constructor. Calls preserve complete caller inputs, and later valid calls recover. Results contain copied payloads without proofs. Ordinary and independently reviewed packages, including standalone result-only packages, passed Node, page, React and worker checks in all three browser engines. Packet is a proof-free object with digit: bigint for Fin 10 and word: bigint for a checked Nat Subtype. The selected adapter descends through Array, List, Option, Product, Except, enclosing Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value field, applies the exact constructor selected for every public site and nested Word field, and leaves the caller's complete rejected graph unchanged. Repeated parameters keep independent constructor choices; later valid calls recover. Copied Array and Option results contain the same nested payload objects without proof fields or input-constructor selection. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices stay in authenticated type metadata and are not host fields. JavaScript and TypeScript pass proof-free objects: On, Off, EmptyToken, UnicodeToken, ZeroToken and WideToken expose count: bigint; Ab exposes size: bigint; EmptySized exposes data: bigint[]. Standalone result-only packages return the same proof-free objects without input-constructor metadata. Proof-only Witness crosses as an owned JavaScript object with no payload properties and as Readonly<Record<PropertyKey, never>> in TypeScript. Token keeps its Unit field, plain empty Marker remains distinct, Option presence, array length and active or inactive Mark branches remain explicit. Full packages validate the nullary checked constructor and exact rejection and recovery; result-only packages project Lean-produced proof-erased values without input-constructor metadata. Packet is a proof-free object with digit: bigint for Fin 10 and word: bigint for a checked Nat Subtype. Repeated parameters keep independent constructor choices; later valid calls recover. Copied Array and Option results contain the same nested payload objects without proof fields or input-constructor selection. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices stay in authenticated type metadata and are not host fields. JavaScript and TypeScript pass proof-free objects: On, Off, EmptyToken, UnicodeToken, ZeroToken and WideToken expose count: bigint; Ab exposes size: bigint; EmptySized exposes data: bigint[]. Standalone result-only packages return the same proof-free objects without input-constructor metadata. Proof-only Witness crosses as an owned JavaScript object with no payload properties and as Readonly<Record<PropertyKey, never>> in TypeScript. Token keeps its Unit field, plain empty Marker remains distinct, Option presence, array length and active or inactive Mark branches remain explicit. Repeated parameters keep independent constructor choices; later valid calls recover. Copied Array and Option results contain the same nested payload objects without proof fields or input-constructor selection. Standalone result-only packages return the same proof-free objects without input-constructor metadata. Installed JavaScript and strict TypeScript callers replay after physical relocation. Chromium, Firefox and WebKit each execute page, React production/Strict Mode and dedicated-worker consumers, including missing-Wasm recovery, for twelve browser executions and fifty-one lifecycle observations. The full package checks direct and repeated parameters plus Array, List, Option, Product, Except, enclosing record and active variant fields; exact failures preserve caller graphs and later calls recover. Producer, browser-consumer and destructive-checker revisions are independently frozen. Nested checked-record acceptance covers only the tested acyclic Packet, Holder and Choice forms through Array, List, Option, Product and Except copy positions. Generic records, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Other host targets require their own installed evidence. These local Linux x64 Node, strict TypeScript, Chromium, Firefox and WebKit runs do not establish hosted acceptance. Constructor dispatch counts and peak memory are unmeasured. Complete npm component/runtime archives and original report inputs are retained; browser binaries, React framework archives and generated deployments are represented by recorded identities and observations rather than copied. Additional inherited browser acceptance: The browser installed lane authenticates the reviewed full inherited checked-record package selection for node-javascript, node-typescript, browser-javascript, browser-react, browser-worker. The full API checks valid, normalized, invalid parent, invalid child, alias, nested Fin, repeated-constructor and recovery cases before projecting proof-free results. Two independent author builds, source removal, offline installation, relocation and unchanged caller replay are retained where the host permits them. The fixture covers inherited parent subobjects, child checked fields, aliases, nested inheritance, repeated constructor selections and constructor-free results. Ordinary and independently reviewed sources are exercised in full and result-only npm packages. Node JavaScript, strict TypeScript, Chromium, Firefox and WebKit execute source-free installed packages; browser contexts cover plain pages, React production and StrictMode, and dedicated workers. Complete component/runtime npm archives, installed receipts, reports, controls, TAP streams and browser observations are retained. Browser binaries and generated deployment directories are represented by their recorded identities and observations. The evidence applies to the exact Linux x64 Node and browser versions recorded in this index. Other hosts require independent installed acceptance. The hosted workflow serializes the four route/mode selections and caps Lean, compiler and build parallelism; peak memory and constructor-dispatch counts are not measured. This archive establishes installed npm/browser behavior, not promotion into the public support inventory. Inherited checked-record acceptance covers only the tested acyclic Span → Ticket → Stamped chain, its Ticket alias, repeated direct parameters, nested parent constraints and proof-free Ticket/Stamped results. Value-carrying receiver-dependent inherited fields, generic or recursive inheritance, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Additional recursive browser acceptance: The browser installed lane authenticates the reviewed mutual recursive checked-record selection for node-javascript, node-typescript, browser-javascript, browser-react, browser-worker. Original inputs, exact failures, preserved rejected values, recovery and proof-free results are retained; independently reproduced packages are installed without author sources and replayed after relocation where the host permits it. The archive authenticates local Linux x64 Node, strict TypeScript, Chromium, Firefox and WebKit execution; it does not claim hosted-runner acceptance. Acceptance covers the tested finite mutually recursive Envelope and Branch records/variants, transparent aliases, Array and Option copies; host cycles are rejected and traversal is bounded. Callback, owned, asynchronous and retained-identity positions remain separate requirements. Browser binaries, framework archives and generated deployments are represented by recorded identities and observations rather than copied. Constructor dispatch counts and peak memory remain unmeasured. Recursive checked-record acceptance covers the tested Packet self-cycle and Envelope ↔ Step mutual cycle, their aliases, Array/Option wrappers, active branches, Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields in copied parameters, results and fields. It does not establish generic recursive records, other recursive graph shapes, value-carrying receiver-dependent fields, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks or owned positions. Additional hosted closed-index acceptance: Hosted GitHub Actions run 39201330491 at 79359306d2e50a5893affe04cafed95d54166b88 rebuilt all four npm/browser selections on Ubuntu 24.04. This full reviewed-ir selection reproduces complete component and shared-runtime npm archives from two author roots, removes author sources, installs offline, relocates the installed tree and replays unchanged Node JavaScript and strict TypeScript callers. chromium 151.0.7922.34, firefox 153.0, webkit 26.5 execute page, React production/StrictMode and dedicated-worker consumers for 12 browser executions and 51 lifecycle observations. The full API exercises all eight checked inputs, exact constructor failures, unchanged rejected values, recovery and all eight proof-free indexed results. The archive authenticates the original workflow, job, artifact, TAP, controls, reports, package receipts and exact source identities. Hosted npm/browser value-index acceptance covers only the archived top-level copied checked-record parameter and result sites with closed Bool, String and Nat indices. Full packages cover parameters and results; standalone result-only packages cover results only. Open or opaque indices; Int, Char, fixed-width and platform-width integers, Fin, functions, proofs, instances and other index kinds; checked-record fields, callbacks and owned positions; value-carrying dependent payloads; and zero-payload checked records remain unreviewed here. Other host targets require separate installed evidence. The Ubuntu 24.04 run records exact Node and browser versions but not peak memory or constructor-dispatch counts. Complete component/runtime npm archives and original workflow records are retained; external toolchains remain trusted recorded inputs. Additional hosted zero-payload npm/browser acceptance: Hosted GitHub Actions run 39588425879 rebuilt the reviewed-ir npm/browser selection on Ubuntu 24.04. Two independent author roots reproduced the complete prepared package before author removal, source-free offline installation and unchanged replay after physical relocation. The package runs the selected nullary Witness constructor at every checked input, keeps rejected values unchanged, recovers on the next valid call and projects proof-erased results. The retained archive authenticates every original artifact byte, route result, caller observation and exact producer, consumer, checker and archiver source closure. Hosted zero-payload npm/Node/browser acceptance covers only the retained Witness, Token, Marker, Option, Array and Mark fixtures at copied parameter and result sites in four ordinary/reviewed full/result-only packages. It does not promote checked-record fields, callbacks, owned positions, other zero-payload shapes, PHP-Wasm or another host. External Lean, consumer-language, package-manager and operating-system toolchains remain trusted recorded inputs. Additional hosted dependent acceptance: Hosted GitHub Actions run 39919381925, job 120300651663, artifact 12491719653 rebuilt the full reviewed-ir node-javascript/node-typescript/browser-javascript/browser-react/browser-worker package selection. The author routes reproduce the package, remove author sources, install without network access and replay unchanged typed callers. The full API exercises valid and rejected dependent inputs through the selected constructor, unchanged rejected values, recovery and proof-free results. The retained archive authenticates every original artifact byte, route result, package, caller observation and selected source. Hosted dependent checked-record acceptance covers only the retained top-level copied DependentRecords.Dependent parameter and result sites, whose Fin bound field depends on the runtime bound field and whose proof is rebuilt by the selected mkDependent constructor. Full packages cover parameters and results; standalone result-only packages cover results only. Dependent fields of other kinds, nested or recursive dependent records, checked-record fields, callbacks, owned positions, open or opaque indices and zero-payload records remain unreviewed here. The PHP-Wasm cells are the shared result tracked by #1461 and are not inferred from native PHP. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs."

Repeated parameters keep independent constructor choices; later valid calls recover. Copied Array and Option results contain the same nested payload objects without proof fields or input-constructor selection. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices stay in authenticated type metadata and are not host fields. Standalone result-only packages return the same proof-free objects without input-constructor metadata. Proof-only Witness crosses as an owned JavaScript object with no payload properties and as Readonly<Record<PropertyKey, never>> in TypeScript. Token keeps its Unit field, plain empty Marker remains distinct, Option presence, array length and active or inactive Mark branches remain explicit. Full packages validate the nullary checked constructor and exact rejection and recovery; result-only packages project Lean-produced proof-erased values without input-constructor metadata. Repeated parameters keep independent constructor choices; later valid calls recover. Copied Array and Option results contain the same nested payload objects without proof fields or input-constructor selection. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices stay in authenticated type metadata and are not host fields. Standalone result-only packages return the same proof-free objects without input-constructor metadata. Proof-only Witness crosses as an owned JavaScript object with no payload properties and as Readonly<Record<PropertyKey, never>> in TypeScript. Token keeps its Unit field, plain empty Marker remains distinct, Option presence, array length and active or inactive Mark branches remain explicit. Full packages validate the nullary checked constructor and exact rejection and recovery; result-only packages project Lean-produced proof-erased values without input-constructor metadata. The proof-free host value carries bound and below as payload fields. Repeated parameters keep independent constructor choices; later valid calls recover. Copied Array and Option results contain the same nested payload objects without proof fields or input-constructor selection. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices stay in authenticated type metadata and are not host fields. Standalone result-only packages return the same proof-free objects without input-constructor metadata. Proof-only Witness crosses as an owned JavaScript object with no payload properties and as Readonly<Record<PropertyKey, never>> in TypeScript. Token keeps its Unit field, plain empty Marker remains distinct, Option presence, array length and active or inactive Mark branches remain explicit. The proof-free host value carries bound and below as payload fields. edits.current: "checked-record": "Pass only payload fields: Interval {lo, hi}, Triple {data} for Sized 3, and Percent {value} for Bounded 0 101, using bigint and bigint[] values. Packet is a proof-free object with digit: bigint for Fin 10 and word: bigint for a checked Nat Subtype. The selected adapter descends through Array, List, Option, Product, Except, enclosing Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value field, applies the exact constructor selected for every public site and nested Word field, and leaves the caller's complete rejected graph unchanged. Repeated parameters keep independent constructor choices; later valid calls recover. Copied Array and Option results contain the same nested payload objects without proof fields or input-constructor selection. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices stay in authenticated type metadata and are not host fields. JavaScript and TypeScript pass proof-free objects: On, Off, EmptyToken, UnicodeToken, ZeroToken and WideToken expose count: bigint; Ab exposes size: bigint; EmptySized exposes data: bigint[]. The full package checks records indexed by both booleans, \"ab\", the empty string, \"λ🌱\", zero and 340282366920938463463374607431768211457 through the exact selected Lean constructors, preserves rejected caller values and recovers on the next valid call. Standalone result-only packages return the same proof-free objects without input-constructor metadata. edits.current: "checked-record": "Pass only payload fields: Interval {lo, hi}, Triple {data} for Sized 3, and Percent {value} for Bounded 0 101, using bigint and bigint[] values. The selected Lean constructor checks or normalizes each input; constructor rejection identifies the parameter and constructor. Calls preserve complete caller inputs, and later valid calls recover. Results contain copied payloads without proofs. Ordinary and independently reviewed packages, including standalone result-only packages, passed Node, page, React and worker checks in all three browser engines. Packet is a proof-free object with digit: bigint for Fin 10 and word: bigint for a checked Nat Subtype. The selected adapter descends through Array, List, Option, Product, Except, enclosing Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value field, applies the exact constructor selected for every public site and nested Word field, and leaves the caller's complete rejected graph unchanged. Repeated parameters keep independent constructor choices; later valid calls recover. Copied Array and Option results contain the same nested payload objects without proof fields or input-constructor selection. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. edits.current: "checked-record": "Pass generated record objects with only payload fields: Interval {lo, hi}, Triple {data} for Sized 3, and Percent {value} for Bounded 0 101. Nat payloads use Brick\\Math\\BigInteger, including small values; data is a consecutive-key array of BigInteger values. Lean runs the constructor selected for each parameter, including normalization. Rejection names the parameter and constructor, preserves complete caller inputs, and permits later valid calls. Results contain copied payloads without proofs. Ordinary, independently reviewed and standalone result-only packages passed weak/strict and startup/lazy Node/Chromium checks on wasm32 PHP 8.4.1. The tested PHP-Wasm Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as Brick\\Math\\BigInteger values. Holder nests Packet, and ChoicePacket carries it in the active Choice branch. Generated PHP-Wasm adapters apply the exact Packet and nested Word constructors selected at each direct, repeated, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder and Choice input site. Rejected calls preserve the complete caller graph and later valid calls recover. Packet arrays and options returned by Lean contain proof-free payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices remain authenticated metadata rather than PHP fields. PHP-Wasm uses `Brick\\Math\\BigInteger` for `count`, `size` and every `EmptySized.data` element on wasm32. Full packages exercise weak and strict PHP callers in Node and Chromium, exact constructor refusals, unchanged rejected values, recovery and proof-free results; standalone result-only packages expose the same copied records without checked-input metadata. Proof-only Witness crosses as a guarded zero-argument readonly PHP class inside wasm32 PHP. Token retains its null Unit field, Marker remains a distinct readonly class, and Option presence, array length and both Mark branches remain distinct. Full Composer and component packages validate the nullary checked constructor, exact-class failures and recovery; result-only packages project Lean-produced proof-erased values without input-constructor metadata. PHP-Wasm represents the tested proof-backed Booking and Claim as generated readonly PHP objects. Window is copied; Claim retains a Ticket owner. Borrowed calls preserve the caller, transferred calls validate before moving the owner, and Lean-produced results omit proofs. The proof-free host value carries bound and below as payload fields. Full packages validate each host input through the selected DependentRecords.mkDependent constructor, which rejects below >= bound before Lean code runs, preserve rejected caller values and return the exact proof-free result. Standalone result-only packages expose Lean-produced results without checked-input metadata."
